pluto.language.markdownDescription: Language of the messages of the extension: labels in hovers and completion, diagnostics, status and output texts. `auto` follows the display language of the editor (Russian for Russian, English otherwise). It changes on the fly. The names and descriptions of settings and commands follow the display language of VS Code itself (command *Configure Display Language*).
pluto.language.enumDescriptions.0: Follow the display language of the editor: Russian if it is Russian, English otherwise.
pluto.lua.enable.markdownDescription: Enable language features (completion, hover, go-to-definition, signature help, outline, and diagnostics) for `.lua` files. Turn this off if another extension, such as `sumneko.lua`, already provides them, to avoid duplicate suggestions. Pluto files still see the declarations of Lua files they use while `#pluto.lua.indexFiles#` is on.
pluto.lua.indexFiles.markdownDescription: Read `.lua` files of the workspace into the index, so that Pluto code can complete, hover and navigate into the Lua modules it `require`s. Independent of `#pluto.lua.enable#`: with that off, Lua files are only read, never decorated with features of their own.
pluto.index.enabled.description: Index all Pluto files of the workspace to provide completion, hover and navigation across files. When disabled, only open files are analyzed.
pluto.index.includeLua.markdownDescripti: Also index `.lua` files, so that Lua modules used from Pluto code are known.
pluto.index.includeLua.markdownDeprecati: Use `#pluto.lua.indexFiles#` instead. When disabled here, `.lua` files are still left out of the index.
pluto.index.exclude.markdownDescription: Glob patterns of files and folders to leave out of the index.
pluto.index.exclude.markdownDeprecationM: Use `#pluto.workspace.exclude#` instead. Patterns set here are still applied.
pluto.workspace.useGitignore.markdownDes: Leave files matched by the `.gitignore` in the root of the workspace folder out of the index. When disabled, `.gitignore` is not read even if it is listed in `#pluto.workspace.ignoreFiles#`.
pluto.workspace.exclude.markdownDescript: Glob patterns of files and folders to leave out of the index, relative to the workspace folder, e.g. `**/vendor/**` or `build/**`. `files.exclude` always applies; `node_modules`, `.git` and `.vs` are always excluded.
pluto.workspace.useSearchExclude.markdow: Also leave out files matched by `#search.exclude#`.
pluto.index.maxFiles.description: Maximum number of files to index per workspace.
pluto.completion.documentWords.descripti: Suggest other words of the current document.
pluto.completion.autoTriggerTypes.markdo: Open the list of types by itself when typing a type hint in a Pluto file: after `:` in `function f(a: `, `function f(): ` and `local x: `. Method calls such as `obj:method` are not affected. The list offers built-in types and the classes of the workspace, each also as nullable (`int?`).
pluto.outline.showFunctionBody.markdownD: Show the contents of functions in the Outline and breadcrumbs: local variables, nested functions and callbacks (and calls, see `#pluto.outline.calls#`). When disabled, only classes, methods and function signatures are shown.
pluto.outline.maxFileLines.markdownDescr: In files with more lines than this, the contents of functions are left out of the Outline to keep the editor responsive, as if `#pluto.outline.showFunctionBody#` was disabled. `0` means no limit.
pluto.outline.calls.markdownDescription: List the calls and `return` statements inside of functions in the Outline, to see what a function does without opening it. At most 50 per function. Requires `#pluto.outline.showFunctionBody#`.
pluto.outline.calls.enumDescriptions.1: List calls that are statements of their own, e.g. `util.toast(...)`, and `return` statements.
pluto.outline.calls.enumDescriptions.2: Also list calls inside of expressions, e.g. `ENTITY.GET_ENTITY_COORDS(...)` in `local coords = v3.new(ENTITY.GET_ENTITY_COORDS(entity))`. Each called function is listed once per function.
pluto.outline.localVariables.description: Show local variables declared inside functions and blocks in the Outline and breadcrumbs. File-level variables are always shown.
pluto.outline.loopVariables.markdownDesc: Show loop variables (`for i = ...`, `for k, v in ...`) in the Outline.
pluto.outline.parameters.description: Show function parameters as children of their function in the Outline.
pluto.outline.anonymousFunctions.markdow: Show anonymous functions and block lambdas, e.g. `scheduler:add() callback`, in the Outline.
pluto.outline.fields.markdownDescription: Show fields assigned via `self.name = ...` as members of their class in the Outline.
pluto.outline.showValues.markdownDescrip: Show the initial value of variables and fields next to their name in the Outline, e.g. `count = 0`.
pluto.hover.sourcePath.markdownDescripti: How hovers and completion details link to a declaration in another file. Declarations in the current file always show just `Line N`.
File name and line, e.g. `VehicleManager.pluto:75`. The full path is shown when pointing at the link.
Path relative to the workspace and line, e.g. `src/lib/game/VehicleManager.pluto:75`.
Don't show where a declaration comes from.
pluto.hover.showFunctionBody.description: Show the source code of a function or method below its signature in hovers: comments removed, indentation normalized and logical blocks separated by blank lines.
pluto.hover.maxBodyLines.markdownDescrip: Longest function source shown in hovers, in lines; longer functions are cut with a `-- ... (+N lines)` note. `0` means no limit. Requires `#pluto.hover.showFunctionBody#`.
pluto.hover.maxDeclarations.description: Number of declarations shown in a hover when several declarations share a name. A link below them opens the list of all.
pluto.highlight.applyColors.markdownDesc: Apply the colors of `pluto.highlight.colors` and `pluto.highlight.tableBracketColors` to Pluto files. The extension keeps them in `editor.tokenColorCustomizations` as rules named `Pluto: ...` and does not touch your other rules; turning this off removes them. Off by default, so the colors of your theme are used.
pluto.highlight.colors.functionName: Names of declared functions and methods.
pluto.highlight.colors.functionKeyword: The `function` keyword and the `->` of lambdas.
pluto.highlight.colors.typeColon: The `:` before a type in a type hint.
pluto.highlight.colors.markdownDescripti: Color and style of each kind of token. Write `{ "color": "#FF8800", "fontStyle": "bold" }` (the color gets a color picker in `settings.json`) or the short form `"#FF8800 bold"`. Styles: `bold`, `italic`, `underline`. Takes effect when `pluto.highlight.applyColors` is on.
pluto.highlight.colors.returnType: The return type of a function: `void` in `function f(): void`, `bool?` in `function f(): bool?`.
pluto.highlight.style.fontStyle: Font style: normal, bold, italic, underline or a combination.
pluto.highlight.tableBracketColors.markd: Colors of the braces `{ }` of tables by nesting depth: the first entry is for the outermost table, the next for the one inside, and so on; the list repeats when it is shorter than the depth (up to 8 levels are told apart). Each entry is written like in `pluto.highlight.colors`, e.g. `[{ "color": "#E6B450" }, { "color": "#59C2FF", "fontStyle": "bold" }]`. Empty by default.
pluto.highlight.style.color: Color for every theme, e.g. `#FF8800`. Click the swatch to pick one. `darkColor` / `lightColor` override it for dark / light themes.
pluto.highlight.style.darkColor: Color for dark and high contrast themes. Falls back to `color`.
pluto.highlight.style.lightColor: Color for light themes (and high contrast light). Falls back to `color`.
pluto.lua.checkSyntax.markdownDescriptio: Check `.lua` files for syntax errors with a Lua interpreter while `pluto.lua.enable` is on. The interpreter is `pluto.lua.compilerPath`, else `luac`, `lua` or `luajit` found in `bin/lua`, `tools/lua` and similar folders of the workspace, else on the `PATH`. The code is only compiled, never run. Without an interpreter only the built-in checks work.
pluto.lua.compilerPath.markdownDescripti: Path to `luac` / `lua` / `luajit` used to check `.lua` files. Supports `${workspaceFolder}`, `${userHome}` and `${env:NAME}`. When empty, the workspace is searched (`bin/lua/luac.exe`, `tools/lua/lua.exe`, ...; the newest version wins), then the `PATH`.
pluto.json.enable.markdownDescription: Check the paths of files written in JSON files (`"entry": "src/main.pluto"`): a path whose file does not exist gets a warning, with a quick fix when the file was moved. Which JSON files are checked is set by `pluto.json.files`.
pluto.json.files.markdownDescription: Glob patterns of the JSON files whose paths are checked, relative to the workspace folder, e.g. `**/info.json`, `config/*.json`, `**/*.json`. The `id`, `entry` and `dependencies` of a module manifest (`info.json`) are always checked.
pluto.json.extensions.markdownDescriptio: Extensions of the files whose paths are checked in the JSON files above. A string is taken for a path only when it ends with one of them (and is not a URL or a pattern).
pluto.json.checkAllPaths.markdownDescrip: Check the paths of files with any extension that exists in the project folder (`.png`, `.txt`, ...), not only those of `pluto.json.extensions`. Needs an open folder: its file names are read once, without the files excluded by `.gitignore`, `.plutoignore`, `.luaignore` and `files.exclude`.
pluto.json.severity.markdownDescription: How a missing file is shown: `warning` (default), `error` or `information`.
pluto.json.notifyNoFolder.markdownDescri: Tell once per window that without an open folder the paths in a JSON file are checked only next to it.
pluto.workspace.ignoreFiles.markdownDesc: Ignore files (`.gitignore` syntax) in the workspace root to read exclusions from: by default `.gitignore`, `.plutoignore` and `.luaignore`. Excluded files are not indexed, so they get no completion or go to definition.
pluto.format.multilineParams.markdownDes: Smart formatting of the parameter list of a function declaration whose `)` is on a line of its own (`.pluto` and `.lua` files): the first parameter typed right after `(` moves to the next line, one level deeper, and Enter at the end of a parameter adds the missing comma and starts the next line with the same indentation. One-line lists are left alone.
pluto.format.multilineTables.markdownDes: Smart formatting of a table whose `}` is on a line of its own (`.pluto` and `.lua` files): the first field typed right after `{` moves to the next line, one level deeper, and Enter at the end of a field adds the missing comma (before a `-- comment`) and starts the next line with the same indentation. One-line tables, and statements inside functions in a table, are left alone.
pluto.highlight.paramNoDefault.markdownD: Underline in yellow the type of the parameter of a function declaration the cursor is on when it has a type but no default value (`function f(test: bool)`). The line goes away when the cursor leaves the parameter or a comma is typed; a tooltip names the values that fit. Pluto files only.
pluto.highlight.paramNoDefaultColor.mark: Color of that line in dark and high contrast themes. Any CSS color, e.g. `#E5C07B`.
pluto.highlight.paramNoDefaultLightColor: Color of that line in light themes.
pluto.completion.defaultValues.markdownD: Suggest the values that can be given to a parameter as its default (`= false`, `= true` for `bool`, `= 0` for `int`, `= nil` for a nullable type, ...) when the cursor is right after its type: `function f(test: bool|)`. Pluto files only.
pluto.completion.defaultValuesDelayMs.ma: Milliseconds the cursor has to rest right after the type of a parameter without a default value before the list of values opens by itself. `0` switches this off; the list can still be opened with `Ctrl+Space`.
pluto.format.newLineAfterComma.markdownD: After a comma typed at the end of an element of a multi-line parameter list or table, start a new line with the indentation of the elements, unless you go on typing (`test: bool = false, test1`) within `pluto.format.newLineAfterCommaDelayMs`. `.pluto` and `.lua` files.
pluto.format.newLineAfterCommaDelayMs.ma: Milliseconds to wait after the comma before the new line starts; typing or moving the cursor cancels it. `0` starts the line at once.
pluto.format.suggestParens.markdownDescr: Show `()` in grey after `function` (also `function name`, `local f = function`); `Tab` inserts it and puts the cursor between the brackets. Nothing is shown when the brackets are already there. If inline suggestions are off (`editor.inlineSuggest.enabled`) it is not shown.
pluto.format.suggestTableKeyAssign.markd: Show ` = ` in grey after the key `["name"]` at the start of a field of a table; `Tab` inserts it.
pluto.format.suggestBlockWords.markdownD: Show ` then` in grey after the header of an `if` / `elseif`, and ` do` after the header of a `while` / `for`; `Tab` inserts it. Enter then adds the `end`.
pluto.format.fixMismatchedBrackets.markd: A closing bracket that does not fit the last opened one (`{ ]`) and matches no other open bracket: `off` ignores it, `suggest` underlines it and offers a quick fix (`Ctrl+.`), `auto` also replaces it by itself when you stop typing for `pluto.format.fixMismatchedBracketsDelayMs`.
pluto.format.fixMismatchedBrackets.sugge: Underline it and offer a quick fix.
pluto.format.fixMismatchedBrackets.auto: Also replace it by itself after a pause.
pluto.format.fixMismatchedBracketsDelayM: Milliseconds to wait before `auto` replaces the closing bracket; typing or moving the cursor cancels it. `0` replaces it at once.
pluto.diagnostics.duplicateParams.markdo: Report a name written twice in the parameters of a function or lambda (`function f(a, a)`) and a key written twice in a table (`{ a = 1, a = 2 }`): `warning` (default), `error` or `off`.
pluto.highlight.nullableTypes.markdownDe: Highlight nullable types (`int?`, `?string`, `Vehicle?`) in type hints of Pluto files.
pluto.highlight.nullableTypeColor.markdo: Color of nullable types in dark and high contrast themes. Any CSS color, e.g. `#FFFFFF`.
pluto.highlight.nullableTypeLightColor.m: Color of nullable types in light themes, where white would be invisible.
pluto.autoCloseBlocks.markdownDescriptio: Insert the matching `end` (or `until`) when pressing Enter after a block opener such as `function`, `if ... then`, `for ... do`, `class` or `switch ... do`.
pluto.diagnostics.enable.markdownDescrip: Show errors and warnings in the editor and the Problems panel: compiler errors (when a Pluto compiler is found, see `#pluto.diagnostics.compilerPath#`) and built-in checks (missing `require` targets, calls with too few arguments, problems in `info.json`).
pluto.diagnostics.compilerPath.markdownD: Path to the Pluto compiler used to check code without running it (`plutoc`, or the `pluto` interpreter). Supports `${workspaceFolder}`, `${userHome}` and `${env:NAME}`. When empty, a compiler inside the workspace is used (e.g. `pluto/*/plutoc.exe`, `tools/pluto/pluto.exe`, `bin/pluto`; the newest version wins), then `plutoc`/`pluto` from `PATH`. If none is found, only the built-in checks run.
pluto.diagnostics.debounceMs.description: Delay in milliseconds after the last edit before a Pluto file is checked again.
